messages:
sam: Quick note 1 opened a docs PR for cobalt-9b model card (https://git.redwood/workspace/docs/pull/834). Found a few discrepancies: JS snippet uses legacy client shape, limits table claims 24k tokens but our perf shows stability to ~18k, bench permalink 404, and no guidance on embedding sharding for ultra-long contexts. Can ppl take pieces?
li: I can update JS snippets to v3. Which import is being used now?
sam: It's `const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk')` which needs to be `import { Client } from '@redwood/sdk'` and `const client = new Client()` for v3. Also the streaming example uses the old event emitter pattern; we should show for-await-of streaming.
anita: I'll handle the limits text. Do you have the perf path?
sam: s3://redwood-bench/cobalt-9b/2026-05/perf.csv. The memory graph hits instability around 18,000 tokens. The model metadata kept upstream ceiling of 24,576. We need to present both clearly.
rahul: For bench link 404, best practice is to link the bench index and include the raw s3 path. That way internal users can follow and external readers see the reproducible location.
anita: Proposed wording: "tested max (tokens): 18,000; catalog ceiling: 24,576 (catalog ceiling is upstream-provided; tested max is from Redwood perf runs)". I'll add a footnote with s3 path and a one-line note that bench index requires internal access.
li: I'll replace snippets with v3 sync + streaming examples and add a small TS embed-shard helper. Draft streaming example: ```ts
import { Client } from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new Client()
const stream = await client.text.stream({ model: 'cobalt-9b' })
await stream.send('Summarize:...')
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta)
}
```
sam: Nice. Can you also include a tiny snippet showing KV/prefix cache hint (TTL guidance) since we've been getting support tickets about cache eviction with long contexts?
li: Yep. I'll add: "Note: prefix cache TTL defaults to 30m; for long-context workflows consider shorter prefix windows or explicit cache keys."
rahul: For embedding sharding guidance I'll add a short recipe: chunk inputs into <=8k token pieces, compute embeddings per chunk, then stitch vectors with chunk offsets in metadata. Suggest shard sizes and parallel requests pattern.
anita: Also add a compatibility bullet: "Quantization variants: q4f16 tested on Dedicated/Private; hosted offers q4a for lower latency. Very long contexts may trigger CPU fallback for q4f16."
sam: One more: benchmarks section states "latency: 150ms @2k" 1 that's median per-token latency, not end-to-end. Change to "median per-token latency (150ms @2k)" to avoid confusion.
li: Pushed snippet commits and the KV cache note. I included both sync/streaming patterns and a TypeScript embed-shard helper.
rahul: I replaced the broken permalink with https://bench.redwood/internal/index and added s3://redwood-bench/cobalt-9b/2026-05/ in the card. Also added a QA item reminding reviewers that the index is internal.
anita: I've updated the limits table and added the footnote. Also added a short supported-variants entry for `cobalt-9b-lite` describing reduced throughput and lower memory footprint.
sam: PR description now has checklist: smoke test snippets with @redwood/sdk@3.6.2, confirm staging render, verify bench index resolves internally. I'll request review once li & anita finish copy edits.
render-bot: preview generated: https://staging.docs.redwood/pr-834 - preview will refresh on new commits.
li: Quick copy edit done; adjusted phrasing on KV cache note and clarified shard example with recommended batch sizes (256-512).
anita: Final pass done on limits footnote and variant table consistency.
sam: All updates are in. If no objections I'll request review by EOD and merge after approvals. Thanks :tada:
